tagline: Up through the orchards and down the old Barlow Road.
intro: Out of Hood River the byway takes OR 35 south up the Hood River Valley among pear, cherry and apple trees, past Parkdale and into the Mt. Hood National Forest. It bends west around the mountain, crosses the White River below the summit and tops Barlow Pass at 4,155 feet, where the Oregon Trail crested the Cascades.

From Government Camp it is downhill on US 26 by Rhododendron, Zigzag, Welches and Brightwood to Sandy and on to Troutdale. Wagons on the old Barlow Road paid a toll of five dollars apiece at first, about a week's wages, for the privilege.

moments.title: Government Camp
moments.text: The only town within five miles of Mount Hood, named for the wagons the Army's Mounted Riflemen had to abandon here in 1849.

moments.title: Timberline Lodge
moments.text: Six twisting miles above Government Camp, the WPA's stone and timber lodge stands at 6,000 feet. Skiing goes on all twelve months. Its exterior played the Overlook Hotel in The Shining.

moments.title: Laurel Hill
moments.text: Travelers counted it the worst stretch of the Oregon Trail, winching wagons down chutes or dragging trees behind for brakes. They named it for its laurels, which were rhododendrons.
